posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Late after sunset in Tanzania’s Serengeti, @maximilian.lehrke watched a lion walk across the dark plains while a line of fire burned in the distance.⁠
⁠
Fire has long been part of life in the Serengeti. While it may look destructive, it clears old, dry grass and helps fresh growth return, which in turn feeds the grazing animals that live here.⁠
⁠
Have you ever seen a wildlife scene this dramatic?

Every winter, the fir trees on Mount Zao in Japan turn into “snow monsters” ❄️⁠
⁠
They’re known as juhyo, and they form when freezing droplets carried by strong winds from the Sea of Japan stick to the branches. Snow keeps piling on top, layer after layer, until the trees are completely covered and take on these strange, giant shapes.⁠
⁠
It only happens when the temperature, wind, and snowfall are just right, and they’re at their best from late January to mid-February. Visitors can see them up c

A daycare for husbands? Copenhagen, you might be onto something. 😂🇩🇰⁠
Want to shop in peace, enjoy some me-time or simply take a break? ⁠
⁠
Drop your husband off at the local “husband daycare” while you enjoy the day. Apparently, they’ve thought of everything!⁠
🎥: @alexisjaneestuart

@vitor.esteves captured the Uros Islands on Lake Titicaca in Peru, where walking feels almost like walking on water.⁠
⁠
Centuries ago, the Uros people moved onto the lake to escape enemies on the mainland, building their own islands by layering totora reeds. Today, homes and schools stand on top of them, and since the reeds slowly rot in the water, new layers have to be added again and again to keep everything afloat.⁠
⁠
Life here isn’t easy, but it’s a beautiful example of a community that lear

A childhood favorite straight from the palm tree. 🌴🤍⁠
Meet the toddy palm, a tropical fruit hiding 2–3 jelly-like seed pods inside its thick outer shell. Its delicate texture is somewhere between coconut flesh and aloe vera, with a mild, refreshing taste that's especially sweet and silky when picked young.⁠
⁠
It's traditionally enjoyed with sweet syrup, but it also makes the perfect tropical dessert with fresh fruit, crushed ice and coconut milk.⁠
A little taste of childhood and a whole lot of

@_goropro_ captured these stunning photos of pigeons in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina.⁠
⁠
Pigeons are so common that we rarely stop to look at them, but up close, their shimmering feathers and bright orange eyes are beautiful. ⁠
⁠
And unlike most birds, they can drink by sucking water up, almost like using a straw, without having to tilt their heads back.⁠

Want to travel more without draining your savings? 🌍

‎Matias left his job at Beautiful Destinations in 2019 and has worked from the road ever since. One thing we’ve learned: you don’t need a 9-5 to travel full-time.

Comment HOTEL to get our list of 500+ hotels that work with creators 🏨

A landscape that looks like it belongs on another planet. 🏜️⁠
China’s Red Mountains are a surreal mix of towering crimson cliffs, unusual rock formations and winding roads cutting through endless shades of red.⁠
⁠
 Almost like driving straight into a different world.⁠
Nature really knows how to create its own masterpieces. 🌍⁠
🎥: @usmanaryan

The Perito Moreno Glacier in Argentina is one of the most impressive sights in Patagonia.⁠
⁠
Its ice wall rises about 70 meters (230 feet) above the water, around the height of a 20-story building, and stretches nearly 3 miles across. It flows from an ice field left over from the last Ice Age, and today visitors can even walk across its surface on guided tours.⁠
⁠
Would you walk on a glacier this big? ⁠
⁠
By: @damexplores

Straight out of a winter fairytale. 😍❄️⁠
The Forest Ice Rink at Okhta Park is the kind of place that makes you want winter to last a little longer. Skate beneath towering, snow-covered fir trees, enjoy the glowing lights, giant Ferris wheel, festive photo spots and cozy corners to warm up between laps.⁠
⁠
A little tip: weekdays are usually less crowded, and Mondays offer free entrance to Okhta Park!⁠
Definitely a winter experience worth adding to your list. ⛸️✨⁠
🎥: @evgeniia_khaibulova

@mseeley20 captured this entire SpaceX Falcon 9 launch in a single photo, using a 426-second exposure.⁠
⁠
Taken from Merritt Island, Florida, it shows the rocket rising over the Banana River, the glowing “jellyfish” plume high in the sky, the booster flying back and landing, and even a special appearance by the International Space Station.⁠
⁠
The rocket was sending a Cargo Dragon full of supplies to the ISS.⁠
⁠
Have you ever seen a rocket launch in person?

Definitely not a hike for the faint-hearted. 😳⛰️⁠
High above the ground, with narrow trails, steep climbs and dizzying drops, this trek at Jebel Jais puts both your physical endurance and mental strength to the test. Every step demands focus, and a fear of heights is certainly not welcome here!⁠
⁠
One of the UAE’s most intense hiking adventures. Would you dare to take it on?⁠
🎥: @shreddedsingh_

Photographer and National Geographic Explorer Morgan Heim (@moheim) captured conservationist Matt Trevelyan walking through the Nidderdale valley in northern England, dressed in a handcrafted Eurasian curlew costume. Trevelyan wears the costume to raise awareness about the near-threatened bird's vanishing habitat in the English moors. He's even worn it on a 53-mile hike and to London's Parliament.

Extreme heat is becoming a fact of life in more parts of the world, with serious implications for pregnant women and their babies.

Hundreds of studies have linked high heat exposure to adverse birth outcomes, but scientists are still trying to figure out just how hot is too hot. A recent study in Sydney is putting that question to the test, using a climate chamber that can reach 104°F (40°C) to determine when pregnant women can no longer safely regulate their core temperature.
